normativeHierarchy.title: The Cool Reference Manual
normativeHierarchy.role: Canonical syntax, typing, built-in class, and operational-semantics source

normativeHierarchy.title: Stanford CS143 reference compiler and runtime documentation
normativeHierarchy.role: Reference behavior for cases not resolved by the language manual

normativeHierarchy.title: Cooler supported language and compatibility contract
normativeHierarchy.role: Explicit project decision for unavailable, nondeterministic, or intentionally out-of-scope compatibility

statusDefinitions.supported: Behavior is claimed and every linked fixture must pass.
statusDefinitions.partial: A tested subset works, while the linked issue tracks missing normative coverage.
statusDefinitions.intentional-divergence: Cooler deliberately differs from the reference behavior and documents the boundary.
statusDefinitions.unsupported: The behavior is outside the current product contract and a linked issue owns reconsideration.
statusDefinitions.not-yet-tested: The behavior is claimed or planned but this corpus does not yet prove it.

manualCoverage.title: Introduction
manualCoverage.rationale: Informative language overview; its concrete class, typing, and runtime claims are specified and mapped by later sections.

manualCoverage.title: Getting Started
manualCoverage.rationale: Ordered source-file compilation is language-visible; MIPS/SPIM artifact compatibility is separately documented as a product boundary.

manualCoverage.title: Classes
manualCoverage.rationale: Class syntax, global names, complete definitions, and whole-program declarations are executable matrix behavior.

manualCoverage.title: Features
manualCoverage.rationale: Attribute and method syntax, formals, uniqueness, and feature typing are exercised positively and negatively.

manualCoverage.title: Inheritance
manualCoverage.rationale: Parent restrictions, acyclicity, inherited attributes, and exact method override signatures are checked.

manualCoverage.title: Types
manualCoverage.rationale: Conformance, static expression types, least upper bounds, and SELF_TYPE are represented in typed-AST and diagnostic evidence.

manualCoverage.title: SELF_TYPE
manualCoverage.rationale: Permitted positions, conformance, new SELF_TYPE, and dynamic/static dispatch result typing are covered.

manualCoverage.title: Type Checking
manualCoverage.rationale: The semantic fixtures prove inferred types and reject unsound programs before lowering.

manualCoverage.title: Attributes
manualCoverage.rationale: Attribute declaration, initializer conformance, defaults, inheritance order, and source-order initialization are covered.

manualCoverage.title: Void
manualCoverage.rationale: Void defaults, isvoid/equality behavior, and the specified dispatch/case failures are executable.

manualCoverage.title: Methods
manualCoverage.rationale: Formal and return contracts, overriding, argument binding, dispatch, and method-body execution are covered.

manualCoverage.title: Expressions
manualCoverage.rationale: All expression grammar families have AST evidence and all expressions receive static types or diagnostics.

manualCoverage.title: Constants
manualCoverage.rationale: Integer, string, and Boolean constants are tokenized, parsed, typed, and boundary checked.

manualCoverage.title: Identifiers
manualCoverage.rationale: Identifier casing, lexical identity, self, lookup, shadowing, and undefined names are covered.

manualCoverage.title: Assignment
manualCoverage.rationale: Right associativity, assignable identifiers, self rejection, conformance, and assignment result typing are covered.

manualCoverage.title: Dispatch
manualCoverage.rationale: Implicit, dynamic, and static dispatch include typing, SELF_TYPE results, evaluation order, selection, and void failure.

manualCoverage.title: Conditionals
manualCoverage.rationale: Bool predicates, selected-branch execution, and least-upper-bound result typing are covered.

manualCoverage.title: Loops
manualCoverage.rationale: Loop grammar, Bool predicates, repeated evaluation, and Object static result are covered.

manualCoverage.title: Blocks
manualCoverage.rationale: Non-empty semicolon-delimited blocks evaluate in order and take the final expression type.

manualCoverage.title: Let
manualCoverage.rationale: Sequential bindings, initialization/defaults, SELF_TYPE positions, conformance, and shadowing are covered.

manualCoverage.title: Case
manualCoverage.rationale: Branch restrictions and joins, most-specific selection independent of source order, void, and no-match behavior are covered.

manualCoverage.title: New
manualCoverage.rationale: Class and SELF_TYPE allocation, typing, defaults, and initializer order are covered.

manualCoverage.title: Isvoid
manualCoverage.rationale: Grammar, Bool static type, and primitive/object/void runtime results are covered.

manualCoverage.title: Arithmetic and Comparison Operations
manualCoverage.rationale: Operand restrictions, precedence, non-associativity, integer arithmetic, ordering, equality, and complements are covered, with overflow explicitly defined by Cooler.

manualCoverage.title: Basic Classes
manualCoverage.rationale: The sealed basic-class prelude and each user-visible method family have executable evidence.

manualCoverage.title: Object
manualCoverage.rationale: Object inheritance plus abort, type_name, and shallow copy contracts are covered.

manualCoverage.title: IO
manualCoverage.rationale: All four IO methods, SELF_TYPE returns, line boundaries, integer parsing, and exhaustion are covered.

manualCoverage.title: Int
manualCoverage.rationale: Int sealing, literal range, default value, signed 32-bit behavior, and arithmetic policy are covered.

manualCoverage.title: String
manualCoverage.rationale: String sealing, constants, defaults, length, concat, substr, and the 1024-character source limit are covered.

manualCoverage.title: Bool
manualCoverage.rationale: Bool sealing, constant casing, default value, equality, condition use, and complement behavior are covered.

manualCoverage.title: Main Class
manualCoverage.rationale: A concrete Main class with a locally defined parameterless main method is required.

manualCoverage.title: Lexical Structure
manualCoverage.rationale: The complete classic lexical surface and its error boundaries are token-level fixtures.

manualCoverage.title: Integers, Identifiers, and Special Notation
manualCoverage.rationale: Identifier classes, decimal integers, punctuation, and multi-character operators have exact token expectations.

manualCoverage.title: Strings
manualCoverage.rationale: Escapes, null/newline/EOF rejection, recovery, decoded values, and length limits are covered.

manualCoverage.title: Comments
manualCoverage.rationale: Line comments, nested block comments, unmatched terminators, and EOF are covered.

manualCoverage.title: Keywords
manualCoverage.rationale: Case-insensitive keywords and the special Boolean initial-letter rule are covered.

manualCoverage.title: White Space
manualCoverage.rationale: The manual whitespace set and line normalization are covered.

manualCoverage.title: Cool Syntax
manualCoverage.rationale: Every production family in the syntax figure is parsed with selected AST-shape evidence.

manualCoverage.title: Precedence
manualCoverage.rationale: Precedence, associativity, dispatch binding, and non-associative comparisons are exact AST/parser evidence.

manualCoverage.title: Type Rules
manualCoverage.rationale: The complete static-semantics families are represented by typed AST observations and ordered diagnostic fixtures.

manualCoverage.title: Type Environments
manualCoverage.rationale: Class, method, and object environments are exercised through inheritance, feature lookup, scopes, and multifile declarations.

manualCoverage.title: Type Checking Rules
manualCoverage.rationale: Each formal expression-rule family has positive inferred-type and negative diagnostic evidence.

manualCoverage.title: Operational Semantics
manualCoverage.rationale: Observable expression values, side effects, dispatch, allocation, case, operators, and specified runtime failures are executed.

manualCoverage.title: Environment and the Store
manualCoverage.rationale: Bindings, assignment, object identity, shallow copying, and evaluation order exercise the observable environment/store model.

manualCoverage.title: Syntax for Cool Objects
manualCoverage.rationale: Basic values, class tags, attribute state, object identity, and void are represented by VM values and built-in behavior.

manualCoverage.title: Class Definitions
manualCoverage.rationale: Inherited/source-order attribute mappings, default initialization, method lookup, and overriding are covered.

manualCoverage.title: Operational Rules
manualCoverage.rationale: Expression evaluation rules and their store/output effects are covered by focused runtime fixtures.

manualCoverage.title: Acknowledgements
manualCoverage.rationale: Credits and bibliography contain no language behavior to implement or test.

claims.contains: | Lexer | Classic identifiers, keywords, literals, nested block comments, line comments, string escapes, diagnostics, and UTF-16-compatible source spans |
| Parser | Classes, features, all documented COOL expression forms, precedence, and recovery with partial artifacts |
| Semantic analysis | Basic-class prelude, inheritance and cycle checks, override rules, scopes, conformance, least upper bounds, `SELF_TYPE`, and `Main.main()` validation |
| Stack IR and control flow | Source-linked executable stack instructions plus basic blocks and CFG edges, verified before VM execution |
| Virtual machine | Object initialization, dynamic/static dispatch, calls, `case`, built-ins, runtime diagnostics, output, and deterministic safety limits |
| Debugger | Incremental phases, source stepping, conditional breakpoints, logpoints, watches, run/pause, reset, trace deltas, stack, frames, and source-linked state |
| Multifile programs | Compiles ordered native source units with stable IDs and file-local spans across every artifact |
| Program input | Line-oriented input from the GUI box or redirected/piped CLI stdin after file arguments |

rules.name: Type and object identifier casing
rules.behavior: ASCII type identifiers start uppercase, ASCII object identifiers start lowercase, and later characters may be letters, digits, or underscore.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the manual's TYPEID and OBJECTID distinction.

rules.name: Case-insensitive keywords
rules.behavior: Keywords are recognized without regard to letter case.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the reference lexer contract.

rules.name: Boolean literal initial casing
rules.behavior: true and false require a lowercase first letter while remaining letters are case-insensitive.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the manual's special Boolean casing rule.

rules.name: Line and nested block comments
rules.behavior: Line comments end at newline and block comments may nest.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the nested block-comment behavior.

rules.name: String characters, escapes, and newline rules
rules.behavior: String literals decode documented controls, ordinary escapes, Unicode characters, and escaped newlines while rejecting unescaped newline, EOF, and null.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the supported manual escape set.

rules.name: Invalid-character diagnostics
rules.behavior: Unrecognized source characters produce stable structured lexer diagnostics.
rules.referenceComparison: Diagnostic identity and structure are Cooler-specific.

rules.name: Rune and UTF-16-compatible source spans
rules.behavior: Token and diagnostic locations preserve line, rune-column, and UTF-16 offsets.
rules.referenceComparison: Browser-compatible offsets are a Cooler tooling extension.

rules.name: Decimal integer literal boundaries
rules.behavior: Unsigned decimal literals accept leading zeroes through 2147483647 and reject larger values without scanner overflow.
rules.referenceComparison: Leading zeroes follow the manual; the 32-bit object-value boundary is enforced before parsing.

rules.name: String length boundary
rules.behavior: Decoded string values contain at most 1024 characters; the first excess character emits one diagnostic and scanning resumes after the closing quote.
rules.referenceComparison: Uses the manual's character count; Unicode storage and offsets are Cooler-defined.

rules.name: ASCII whitespace and newline conventions
rules.behavior: Space, LF, form feed, CR, tab, and vertical tab are ignored; CRLF is one source line break.
rules.referenceComparison: The whitespace set matches the manual; unified CR/LF source lines are a Cooler location decision.

rules.name: Punctuation and longest-match operators
rules.behavior: Every punctuation token is recognized and <=, <-, and => take precedence over their single-character prefixes.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the manual's special notation.

rules.name: UTF-8 decoding and ASCII lexical grammar
rules.behavior: Unicode is accepted inside strings, non-ASCII grammar runes are rejected, and malformed UTF-8 bytes receive a distinct deterministic diagnostic.
rules.referenceComparison: UTF-8 decoding is a Cooler source-format contract beyond the ASCII manual.

rules.name: Recoverable lexical errors
rules.behavior: Invalid identifiers, characters, integers, and strings preserve deterministic later tokens without diagnostic cascades.
rules.referenceComparison: Recovery token values and structured diagnostic identities are Cooler-specific.

rules.name: Classes and features
rules.behavior: Programs contain complete class declarations with method and attribute features.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the documented class and feature grammar.

rules.name: Assignment syntax
rules.behavior: Assignments require an object identifier on the left and associate right-to-left.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the manual assignment form and precedence.

rules.name: Dispatch syntax
rules.behavior: Implicit-self, dynamic, and static dispatch parse with bounded argument lists.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the manual dispatch forms.

rules.name: Conditional syntax
rules.behavior: Conditional expressions require then, else, and fi delimiters.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the manual conditional grammar.

rules.name: Loop syntax
rules.behavior: Loop expressions require loop and pool delimiters.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the manual loop grammar.

rules.name: Block syntax
rules.behavior: Blocks are non-empty and every contained expression ends with a semicolon.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the manual block grammar.

rules.name: Let syntax
rules.behavior: Let expressions parse one or more ordered typed bindings and an in body.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the documented let form.

rules.name: Case syntax
rules.behavior: Case expressions parse typed, semicolon-terminated branches between of and esac.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the documented case form.

rules.name: Allocation, unary, arithmetic, and comparison syntax
rules.behavior: new, isvoid, complement, arithmetic, and comparison expressions parse.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the documented expression inventory.

rules.name: Expression precedence and associativity
rules.behavior: Dispatch, unary, multiplicative, additive, comparison, not, and assignment precedence is preserved.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the precedence table selected by the project.

rules.name: Non-associative comparisons
rules.behavior: Chained comparison operators are rejected unless explicitly parenthesized.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the manual's non-associative comparison rule.

rules.name: Parser recovery with partial artifacts
rules.behavior: Parser errors preserve deterministic diagnostics and partial syntax artifacts where possible.
rules.referenceComparison: Recovery shape is Cooler-specific and not byte-compatible with coolc.

rules.name: Class inheritance and cycles
rules.behavior: Reserved and duplicate declarations, default inheritance, forbidden or undefined parents, and independent cycles are checked in deterministic source order with safe recovery.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the class hierarchy restrictions.

rules.name: Attribute, method, and formal declarations
rules.behavior: Attribute, method, formal, initializer, and method-body declarations enforce naming, uniqueness, defined types, and conformance.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the manual feature declaration and typing rules.

rules.name: Inherited attributes and exact method overrides
rules.behavior: Inherited attributes cannot be redefined and overriding methods preserve every formal and return type exactly.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the manual's feature inheritance rules.

rules.name: Main.main entry point
rules.behavior: A runnable program declares (rather than inherits) Main.main with no formal parameters, a defined return type, and a conforming body.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches reference program startup requirements.

rules.name: Assignment typing
rules.behavior: Assignments reject self and unknown targets, enforce value conformance, and preserve the right-hand static type.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the formal assignment typing rule.

rules.name: Dispatch typing
rules.behavior: Implicit, dynamic, and static dispatch enforce receiver conformance, method existence, arity, argument types, and SELF_TYPE substitution.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the formal dispatch typing rules.

rules.name: Conditional and loop typing
rules.behavior: Conditions are Bool, conditional branches use LUB, and while has type Object.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the manual type rules.

rules.name: Let scopes, conformance, and defaults
rules.behavior: Let bindings introduce ordered scopes, enforce conformance, and receive type defaults without initializers.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the documented default initialization and typing.

rules.name: Case typing and branch restrictions
rules.behavior: Case branches use distinct concrete types and the result uses their least upper bound.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the case typing rule.

rules.name: SELF_TYPE conformance
rules.behavior: SELF_TYPE preserves the receiver's dynamic family through conformance, LUB, allocation, assignment, and dispatch substitution while obeying restricted declaration positions.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the supported SELF_TYPE typing rules.

rules.name: Integer and Boolean complement typing
rules.behavior: Integer complement accepts Int and Boolean not accepts Bool.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the formal complement typing rules.

rules.name: Arithmetic operand typing
rules.behavior: All arithmetic operators require two Int operands and produce Int.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the formal arithmetic typing rule.

rules.name: Comparison and equality typing
rules.behavior: Ordering requires Int operands while equality restricts comparisons involving Int, String, or Bool to the same basic type.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the formal comparison and equality typing rules.

rules.name: Lexical scopes and shadowing
rules.behavior: Identifiers resolve through attribute, formal, let, and case scopes with deterministic inner shadowing.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the manual lexical-scope rules.

rules.name: Declared type conformance
rules.behavior: Initializer, method body, assignment, and argument static types conform to their declarations before lowering.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the manual conformance relation.

rules.name: Object allocation, initialization, and copying
rules.behavior: Allocation installs defaults, evaluates inherited then local initializers in source order, and copy preserves dynamic type with shallow fields.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches observable reference allocation and initialization semantics.

rules.name: Dynamic/static dispatch and evaluation order
rules.behavior: Arguments evaluate left-to-right before the receiver, dynamic dispatch selects the runtime method, and static dispatch selects the named ancestor implementation.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches observable reference dispatch semantics.

rules.name: Closest case branch selection
rules.behavior: case selects the closest conforming branch for the runtime type.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the reference case-selection rule.

rules.name: Runtime arithmetic
rules.behavior: Arithmetic evaluates operands left-to-right and produces signed Int results; division truncates toward zero.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches observable reference arithmetic except overflow, tracked separately.

rules.name: Runtime comparison and equality categories
rules.behavior: Ordering compares Int values; equality compares basic values, non-basic object identity, and void by their COOL categories.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches observable reference comparison and equality semantics.

rules.name: Runtime complements and isvoid
rules.behavior: Integer complement, Boolean not, and isvoid evaluate once and produce the specified Int or Bool result.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches observable reference complement and isvoid semantics.

rules.name: Arithmetic runtime failures
rules.behavior: Division by zero halts with one stable user-runtime diagnostic.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the manual failure condition; diagnostic structure is Cooler-specific.

rules.name: Dispatch runtime failures
rules.behavior: Dispatch on void halts before method entry with one stable user-runtime diagnostic.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the manual failure condition; diagnostic structure is Cooler-specific.

rules.name: Case runtime failures
rules.behavior: Case on void and case without a conforming branch halt with distinct stable diagnostics.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the manual failure conditions; diagnostic structure is Cooler-specific.

rules.name: Built-in runtime failures
rules.behavior: Object.abort and invalid String.substr bounds halt with distinct stable diagnostics.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the manual failure conditions; diagnostic structure is Cooler-specific.

rules.name: Deterministic VM safety limits
rules.behavior: Execution pauses, halts, or evicts retained state deterministically at every documented instruction, stack, call, scope, allocation, trace, string, output, input, and breakpoint bound.
rules.referenceComparison: These deterministic educational limits are Cooler-specific.

rules.name: Deterministic signed 32-bit integer semantics
rules.behavior: Int values are signed 32-bit two's-complement values; arithmetic and complement wrap modulo 2^32, MIN/-1 yields MIN, and input outside the signed range yields zero.
rules.referenceComparison: The manual does not specify overflow. Cooler makes the classic 32-bit representation architecture-independent with an explicit modular policy; differential reference execution requires an optional local toolchain.

rules.name: Basic-class prelude
rules.behavior: Object, IO, Int, String, and Bool are available with the documented inheritance relationships.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the declared basic-class surface.

rules.name: Object methods
rules.behavior: abort, type_name, and copy expose the documented observable behavior.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches observable behavior; allocation identity is Cooler-internal.

rules.name: IO methods and supplied program input
rules.behavior: IO output methods append text and input methods consume supplied lines deterministically; Int input and output use signed 32-bit decimal semantics.
rules.referenceComparison: Method values match; input delivery and deterministic out-of-range recovery are adapted to local GUI/CLI execution.

rules.name: String methods
rules.behavior: length, concat, and substr operate on Unicode code points, with overflow-safe bounds checks and stable failures.
rules.referenceComparison: The manual specifies characters without an encoding model; Cooler explicitly extends classic ASCII sources with Unicode code-point behavior.

rules.name: Educational backend artifacts
rules.behavior: Successful programs produce mutually consistent stack IR, control flow, and pseudo-assembly artifacts that pass bytecode verification before VM execution.
rules.referenceComparison: Artifacts are intentionally Cooler-specific rather than MIPS/SPIM output.

rules.name: Source-level debugger behavior
rules.behavior: Incremental phases, breakpoints, step, run/pause, reset, and trace deltas remain deterministic.
rules.referenceComparison: Cooler exposes its own debugger protocol and controls. Machine-readable scenarios exercise bounded debugger actions and stable snapshot fields.

rules.name: Ordered multifile compilation
rules.behavior: Complete classes from source files are compiled in argument order as one program.
rules.referenceComparison: Matches the reference compiler's ordered whole-program class semantics while retaining native source origins.

rules.name: Native SourceUnit multifile identity
rules.behavior: The result contract and every source-linked artifact preserve stable source-unit identity with file-local coordinates.
rules.referenceComparison: Cooler-specific artifact identity; observable whole-program behavior remains comparable to the reference toolchain.

rules.name: Reference MIPS/SPIM ABI compatibility
rules.behavior: Cooler does not emit reference MIPS object layout, assembly, linker inputs, or SPIM executables.
rules.referenceComparison: Explicit non-goal; Cooler uses educational stack bytecode and a Go VM. The optional local differential harness compares observable acceptance and runtime behavior without claiming ABI compatibility.

divergence.boundary: Generated stack bytecode, pseudo-assembly, object layout, calling convention, and packages are Cooler-native and are not MIPS/SPIM artifacts.
divergence.reason: The product is a portable educational compiler lab with an inspectable Go VM, not a replacement for the historical CS143 backend toolchain.
divergence.consequence: Users cannot link Cooler output with reference runtime objects or execute its pseudo-assembly in SPIM; only normalized source acceptance and observable program behavior are comparable.
divergence.assertion: README-BACKEND and TOOL-BACKEND-ARTIFACTS claims plus artifact-contract tests prevent pseudo-assembly from being represented as reference assembly.

rules.name: Modules and separate compilation
rules.behavior: Imports, modules, split class declarations, object files, and linking are not supported.
rules.referenceComparison: Explicit non-goal: the COOL manual defines programs as sets of complete classes, not modules.

divergence.boundary: A project is an ordered set of complete class declarations; imports, module declarations, split classes, object files, and separate linking do not exist.
divergence.reason: Those constructs are language extensions absent from classic COOL and would change parsing, name resolution, and project semantics.
divergence.consequence: Users must pass all complete source units together and cannot publish or link separately compiled modules.
divergence.assertion: README-PARSER and README-MULTIFILE claims are audited against PAR-PROGRAM-STRUCTURE and TOOL-MULTIFILE, whose fixtures reject incomplete/split declarations and preserve ordered whole-program semantics.

rules.name: Deterministic and explicit interactive input modes
rules.behavior: Supplied input is finite and deterministic; explicit CLI and GUI interaction waits before each exhausted input opcode, accepts one sequenced line, and preserves reset and reverse-replay semantics.
rules.referenceComparison: Builtin return values follow the documented COOL surface; source/program channel separation, explicit interaction, sequencing, and replay are Cooler-specific host protocols.
